headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, clipboard, screenshots, and app context, while Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes. If Flowise outputs are copied into ChatGPT or files are shared, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or chatflow output that is then opened in ChatGPT Desktop
IF the operator copies Flowise output into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the two agents
Use a read-only staging folder for any exchanged files
Add a manual provenance check before ChatGPT follows any instruction-like text
requires-engineering: enforce content tagging or provenance metadata across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and Flowise reads/writes server files plus sends data to model providers and configured HTTP/search tools. In a shared workspace, sensitive content can flow from ChatGPT into Flowise and then out through broad egress, creating exfiltration risk in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files
IF a Flowise flow forwards file contents or chatflow inputs to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces or containers
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory before running Flowise
Restrict Flowise tool nodes to approved endpoints only
Turn off uploads for sensitive documents in ChatGPT Desktop for this workflow
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting at the deployment layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access and no write or git mutation, while Flowise can write the server filesystem. That reduces direct write-write conflict, but both can still contend over shared files in a common workspace, especially because Flowise state is shared via server datastore and ChatGPT can read local files. The overlap is real in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Flowise flows modify files that ChatGPT Desktop is simultaneously reading
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use file locks or a simple check-in/check-out convention
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as tool inputs, and ChatGPT Desktop can generate content from files, screenshots, and app context. If ChatGPT output is fed into Flowise without verification, Flowise may execute or route it as authoritative workflow data, causing downstream actions based on untrusted text. The pair therefore has a strong default cascade path.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop output is pasted or imported into a Flowise node without validation
IF a Flowise flow uses that output to trigger API calls or browser actions
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Flowise consumes ChatGPT output
Require structured schemas for any handoff payloads
Limit Flowise actions to dry-run mode for the first pass
Log and diff upstream text before execution
requires-engineering: add validation nodes that reject free-form instructions

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can process uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Flowise stores chatflow inputs/outputs and may persist server-side data. If regulated data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge even though the profiles do not specify a named regime. The mismatch is plausible enough to warrant medium severity, not none.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or customer secrets are entered into both agents
IF Flowise deployment retention differs from ChatGPT Desktop or connected-service retention
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Purge Flowise chatflow logs after each run
Confirm retention settings for both systems before use
Use synthetic or redacted test data
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across deployments
